title: Regional control-plane split with telemetry gateway reference
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview
======

This page describes a reference architecture for splitting the Redwood private control plane across multiple regions and colocating a telemetry gateway to minimize sensitive telemetry egress, reduce cross-region latency, and support regulated VPC and air-gapped deployments. The pattern is intended for customers that require: regional control-plane autonomy, bounded telemetry flow, and predictable failover semantics for inference-serving workloads.

Goals
-----

- Keep control-plane decisions local to reduce cross-region dependence for runtime routing and tenant configuration.
- Provide a telemetry gateway that aggregates, sanitizes, and routes observability data under customer-controlled contracts.
- Enable cross-region failover with deterministic state reconciliation and minimal model-availability disruption.
- Preserve auditability and evidence retention for compliance reviews.

When to use this pattern
------------------------

Use this architecture when customers request any of the following: VPC-level data residency, limited egress for telemetry, independent regional SLA targets, or geographic separation to satisfy regulatory constraints. Do not use for very small single-region deployments where the added complexity outweighs benefits.

Architecture summary
--------------------

High-level components:

1. Regional control plane instance per region (RCP): manages tenant config, model pinning decisions, rollout policies, and routing hints. RCP instances are authoritative for the tenants assigned to that region.
2. Telemetry gateway (TG): a lightweight aggregation tier deployed at the regional boundary or in a customer-managed VPC. TG performs sampling, PII redaction, PII-aware hashing, rate limiting, and local buffering before forwarding to the central observability sink or customer SIEM.
3. Regional model store (RMS): cached model artifacts and quantized variants co-located with serving to speed cold starts and model swaps.
4. Cross-region synchronizer: a limited-state, append-only log for control-plane deltas needed for failover (tenant assignment, model index, KV cache checkpoints). Designed for eventual consistency with explicit reconciliation windows.

Diagram (text)
--------------

Region A: RCP-A  <--- private RPCs --->  Serving-A  <--- local RMS-A
                 |
                 +---> TG-A --> Central observability or customer SIEM (filtered)
                 |
                 +---> cross-region sync --> RCP-B

Region B: RCP-B  <--- private RPCs --->  Serving-B  <--- local RMS-B

Key design decisions
--------------------

- Control-plane split: RCPs own tenant assignment; global control is limited to an orchestration coordinator that holds policy but not tenant-level secrets. This minimizes blast radius for cross-region network failures.
- Telemetry gating: All telemetry leaving a region must pass through TG which is controlled by the deployment operator. TG enforces labeling, PII redaction, sampling, and egress allowlists.
- Minimal sync surface: The cross-region synchronizer only replicates the fields required for safe failover: tenant id -> active region, stable model index, last successful model artifact checksum, and a monotonic checkpoint id for KV cache snapshots.

SLOs and constraints
--------------------

- Regional control-plane availability: 99.95% per region (target).
- Telemetry delivery latency to central sink: 30s 95th percentile after TG processing (configurable).
- Failover reconvergence: < 120s for control-plane failover upon region loss, without data loss for stateless requests.
- KV cache warmup for model swap: aim for 30s to 3x baseline latency spike depending on model size.

Hardware, network, and KMS requirements (table)
-----------------------------------------------

| Component | Minimum spec | Notes |
|-----------|--------------|-------|
| RCP instances | 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM | Small fleet for HA; scale by tenant count |
| Telemetry gateway | 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM | Must be network-adjacent to serving plane for low latency |
| RMS storage | 1 TB NVMe per 100 concurrent models | Use encrypted volumes and signed artifacts |
| KMS/HSM | Customer-controlled KMS endpoint | TLS mutual auth; support for envelope encryption |
| Network | 10 Gbps internal, private peering between regions | BGP or cloud backbone recommended |

Network ports and firewall rules (short)
---------------------------------------

- Control plane API: TCP 8443 inbound from serving plane only
- TG ingestion: TCP 8088 (TLS) inbound from serving nodes
- Cross-region sync: TCP 9090 (mutual TLS) outbound to peer RCPs
- Artifact pull: HTTPS 443 outbound to RMS mirrors

Operational playbooks
---------------------

A. Tenant regional bind and canary activation

1. Preflight: run tenant-readiness-check.sh which validates RMS artifact presence, KMS connectivity, and TG allowlist entries.
2. Update desired assignment in orchestration coordinator. The coordinator emits a signed delta; RCP in target region validates and accepts.
3. Canary traffic: enable 1% of requests routed to target region via traffic-steering policy. Monitor latency, error rate, and token cost for 15 minutes.
4. Full roll: increase traffic to 100% in 6 linear increments, validating at each step.

B. Control-plane regional failover (operator-initiated)

1. Trigger: detected region outage or scheduled evacuation.
2. Promote backup RCP: set active region marker for affected tenants via orchestration coordinator, with a monotonic checkpoint id.
3. RMS validation: ensure RMS in promoted region has required artifacts; if missing, trigger artifact fetch from upstream archive with prioritized pull.
4. KV cache restore: restore latest KV snapshot for tenant; if snapshot not present, use warm start strategy and enforce degraded inference SLOs.
5. Confirm traffic shift and monitor for anomalies for 10 minutes.

C. Telemetry gateway incident: data loss suspected

1. TG operator sets ingest to buffer-only mode and writes a timed marker event to local durable store.
2. If data can be reconstructed from local buffers, replay to central sink following the dedupe window.
3. If not reconstructable, promote next-level sampling summary and notify compliance lead with an evidence bundle.

Upgrade and rollback procedure (control-plane components)
--------------------------------------------------------

Principles:
- Blue-green for RCP: always upgrade a standby fleet and perform traffic cutover after health checks.
- Telemetry gateway: rolling upgrades with stateful drain, use buffer and replay mechanisms.
- Cross-region synchronizer: upgrades are backward compatible for at least two versions.

Controlled upgrade steps:
1. Create blue standby in region and seed with current config and latest delta log.
2. Smoke test API endpoints and run workload simulator against standby at 20% of production QPS.
3. Swap leadership via orchestration coordinator and monitor for 15 minutes.
4. If errors exceed thresholds (error rate > 0.5% or tail latency increase > 40%), rollback using recorded standby snapshot and revert leadership marker.

Rollback playbook highlights:
- Preserve delta logs and checksums to avoid split-brain.
- Do not perform cross-region rollback simultaneously; stagger by region.
- If rollback fails due to data schema mismatch, initiate emergency compatibility mode: accept both old and new delta formats for 2 hours and notify engineering.

Day-2 operational checks and metrics
----------------------------------

Essential dashboards and alerts:
- RCP health: CPU, memory, API 5xx rate, control-plane operation latency.
- TG throughput and drop rate, PII redaction successes, buffer fill percentage.
- Cross-region sync lag and last checkpoint id per tenant.
- RMS artifact consistency: checksum mismatch alerts.

Suggested alert thresholds:
- RCP 5xx rate > 0.2% sustained for 5 minutes
- TG buffer fill > 70% for 10 minutes
- Cross-region sync lag > 60s per tenant

Compliance and evidence preservation
----------------------------------

- All region-to-region deltas must be signed and stored in an append-only evidence store for a minimum of 180 days by default.
- TG must retain redaction logs and sampling decisions tied to tenant ids for audit windows defined in the customer contract.
- Provide automated evidence bundles for QBRs: include delta logs, artifact checksums, TG ingest summaries, and canary run metrics.

Acceptance checklist for field installation
-----------------------------------------

- [ ] KMS endpoint reachable and verified with test envelope decryption
- [ ] RMS contains signed artifacts for all tenant pinned models
- [ ] Telemetry gateway allowlist and redaction policy loaded and smoke-tested
- [ ] Cross-region peering and mutual TLS validated with sample delta exchange
- [ ] Synthetic workload confirms < 3x baseline tail latency for cold-starts

References and related reading
----------------------------

- See cross-region synchronizer implementation notes in the runtime repo for delta schema.
- TG redaction policy format: policy-v2.yaml example in ops-configs.
- Tenant assignment and SLA decomposition playbook in day-2-ops.

Owner and maintenance
---------------------

Owner: eng-private-deployments architecture team
Maintainers: runtime-ops, telemetry-ops
Review cadence: architecture review every 6 months or after any regulatory change

Appendix: example CLI snippets
-----------------------------

1) Validate KMS connectivity

$ redwoodctl kms test --endpoint https://kms.customer.example --key-id projects/123/keys/abc

2) Emit signed tenant assignment delta

$ redwoodctl control assign-tenant --tenant-id tenant-42 --region us-west-2 --sign-key /etc/creds/orch-key.pem

3) Check cross-region sync lag (quick)

$ curl -s https://rcp-us-west-2.internal:9090/metrics | jq '.sync_lag["tenant-42"]'
